hints: Follow each starting alkene through its own reaction sequence separately, starting with what type of addition or cleavage happens first.
Ethene to ethanol to full oxidation under reflux gives a 2-carbon carboxylic acid, so work out its formula and functional group.
Hot concentrated manganate(VII) cleaves the C=C bond in but-2-ene completely, so count the carbons in each fragment and compare its functional group to X.
walkthrough:
**Find X from ethene**

Think of this as hydration then strong oxidation. Ethene adds steam to make ethanol.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. H}_3\text{PO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Oxidise ethanol fully under reflux**

A primary alcohol with acidified dichromate(VI) under reflux is oxidised all the way, first to ethanal then to ethanoic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{[O], \text{reflux}} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$ 
So X is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, ethanoic acid, with 2 carbons and a carboxylic acid group.

**Find Y from but-2-ene**

Hot, concentrated, acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ does oxidative cleavage. It breaks the C=C bond completely.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. MnO}_4^- / \text{H}^+} \text{organic acids}$$

**Compare X and Y**

But-2-ene is symmetrical: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=$ on each side. Each $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=$ fragment is oxidised to $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$ 
So Y is also ethanoic acid. Same formula, same 2 carbons, same functional group as X.

options.A: Incorrect. X is ethanoic acid with 2 carbons. Y is also ethanoic acid with 2 carbons, so X does not have more carbons.
options.B: Incorrect. Although but-2-ene starts with 4 carbons, the C=C bond is cleaved. Each product molecule Y has only 2 carbons, the same as X.
options.C: Incorrect. Both X and Y are carboxylic acids ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$). Students sometimes think cleavage gives a ketone or aldehyde, but hot concentrated conditions give the acid.
options.D: Correct. X is ethanoic acid from full oxidation of ethanol, and Y is ethanoic acid from cleavage of but-2-ene. Both are the same compound.
